literal_source_claim_zh: 线性系统的稳定性判据
literal_source_claim_en: A stability criterion for linear systems.
source_attribution: many mathematicians, twentieth century (catalog metadata only)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a source-selected linear dynamical system, characterize the source-selected stability notion by the exact spectral, semigroup, Lyapunov, coefficient, or other conditions stated in that source.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix continuous or discrete time, autonomous or time-varying dynamics, homogeneous or input-output form, finite- or infinite-dimensional state space, scalar field, solution model, equilibrium, stability notion, criterion family, direction of implication, quantifier order, or boundary cases. Even for a finite-dimensional continuous-time autonomous system, bounded stability and asymptotic or exponential stability have different spectral criteria. Selecting one familiar variant would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix the time monoid or field, state and scalar spaces, dimension, topology and norm, system matrix or operator family, initial-value or input-output solution carrier, equilibrium, and all universes and typeclass assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose bounded, Lyapunov, asymptotic, exponential, uniform, marginal, BIBO, input-to-state, or another stability notion, nor a one-way sufficient condition or an if-and-only-if classification.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every boundary case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: finite-dimensional continuous-time autonomous bounded stability characterized by nonpositive eigenvalue real parts and semisimple imaginary-axis eigenvalues
finite-dimensional continuous-time autonomous asymptotic or exponential stability characterized by strictly negative eigenvalue real parts
finite-dimensional discrete-time stability characterized by unit-disk spectral conditions with the appropriate boundary semisimplicity clause
a continuous-time Lyapunov matrix inequality equivalent to Hurwitz stability
uniform exponential stability of a nonautonomous fundamental matrix or an infinite-dimensional semigroup
BIBO or input-to-state stability of a controlled linear system
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero-dimensional state space, zero matrix or operator, identity dynamics, and zero initial condition
eigenvalues on the imaginary axis or unit circle, including defective Jordan blocks
repeated eigenvalues, nondiagonalizable and nonnormal operators, and real versus complex spectral encodings
finite-time, forward-time, two-sided-time, local, global, uniform, and nonuniform notions
time-varying coefficients, switching, forcing, inputs, outputs, delays, and affine terms
unbounded generators, residual or continuous spectrum, domain density, and semigroup well-posedness
equilibrium at zero versus an arbitrary equilibrium and any coordinate translation
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1342 general Lyapunov stability theory or THM-M-1344 transfer from a nonlinear linearization
THM-M-1356 Routh-Hurwitz coefficient criterion or THM-M-1357 Nyquist input-output criterion
THM-M-1352 through THM-M-1354 periodic-coefficient Floquet theory, its theorem, or characteristic exponents
continuous-time Hurwitz stability silently substituted for a discrete-time, time-varying, semigroup, or controlled-system claim
asymptotic or exponential stability substituted for bounded or Lyapunov stability, or conversely
matrix exponential, eigenvalue, spectrum, Jordan-form, ODE, or norm APIs alone
a structure field or hypothesis that directly assumes the requested stability or criterion equivalence
a numerical eigenvalue computation, simulated trajectory, plot, or floating-point stability classification
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe used as proof credit
